title: Artin join theorem for local integral algebras over henselizations
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p_1,\mathfrak p_2\subset A$ prime ideals, and $D_i$ local commutative $A^h_{\mathfrak p_i}$-algebras integral over $A^h_{\mathfrak p_i}$, for $i=1,2$. Here $A^h_{\mathfrak p}$ means the henselization of $A_{\mathfrak p}$: the henselian local ring with its universal local map from $A_{\mathfrak p}$ (initial among local maps from $A_{\mathfrak p}$ to henselian local rings). For a ring $T$ and a connected component $Z$ of $\operatorname{Spec}T$, write $T_Z=T/I_Z$, where $I_Z$ is generated by the idempotents $e$ such that $Z\subseteq V(e)$; this is the component ring. Integral means that every element satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in the source ring. A ring is quasi-acyclic when all its component rings are henselian local [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Then $E=D_1\otimes_A D_2$ is quasi-acyclic. For any component ring $C$ of $E$, let $\mathfrak m_C$ be its unique maximal ideal. If both maps $D_i\to C$ are nonlocal, then $C/\mathfrak m_C$ is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed]. If $D_i\to C$ is local for an index $i$, then this map is integral and $C/\mathfrak m_C$ is algebraic [def-weil-algebraic-element] over $D_i/\mathfrak m_{D_i}$. A homomorphism of local rings is local when the inverse image of the target maximal ideal is the source maximal ideal.
